page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Rachel the rabbit!
title: Rachel the rabbit!
topic: Language for dealing with a difficult colleague
description:
Anna is struggling to work with Rachel, Mr Socrates' favourite Sales Executive. Rachel was sent to help out but she is becoming more of a hindrance and Anna has to deal with it. What will she say?
This episode focuses on what to say when you have to deal with a difficult person at work.
phrases: I'm concerned that she's made a mistake that might affect the business.
I'm finding it very difficult to work with her.

listening_challenge.question: How does Tom describe Rachel to Anna?
listening_challenge.answer: He says she's a bit of a man-eater.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello. It's another busy day at the offices of Tip Top Trading…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: And I said no John, not at my age, I'd rather take the bus…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …yeah Pete, that's great, so we'll deliver 2,000 bananas by Friday. Let's have a beer soon… yeah… cheers mate.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: But there are two people who are busy annoying each other…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: So you did what? You ordered the second-hand ones?!

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Chillax Hannah…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Anna!

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: …they're just oranges…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …plastic lemons actually.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna is struggling to work with Rachel, Mr Socrates' favourite Sales Executive, who he's sent in to help out… or hinder more like!

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Look, I'm off for a cappuccino, everything will be just fine. Ciao.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Anna, has Rachel gone out?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: She's a bit of a man-eater. She almost ate me once.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: She eats men?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Well, not exactly. I worked with her in my last job. She was always listening in to other people's conversations and she's always changing jobs. That's why they call her Rachel Rabbit – you know, big ears, always jumping from one job to another.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Rachel Rabbit! That's funny. So she isn't that good then?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh, useless! She only worked for Mr Socrates because her father threatened to sue the company, after one of our plastic pineapples fell off a shelf and broke his toe. But, better keep that under your hat.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: My hat?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: I mean, keep it secret.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh right, I see. Well, now she's ordered loads of second-hand oranges to send to our new customer in France.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: But they wanted Imperial Lemons?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I know. I'm not sure what to do, so I'm going to have to speak to Paul about this.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes it's a good idea to refer up sometimes – ask the boss for advice. Say to him "I'm concerned that Rachel has made a mistake that might affect the business". You might also say "she's not pulling her weight", meaning she's not doing the work she is supposed to do. And you could say "I'm finding it very difficult to work with this person."

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. I'll try. There's Paul now… Paul, could I have a word please?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Of course, Anna. Let's go in my office. Now, how can I help?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, well, it's Rachel.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, amazing woman. Mr Socrates' favourite.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I know… but I'm finding it difficult to work with her.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh why's that?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I'm a bit concerned that she's made a mistake and it might affect our business.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Golly gosh. Really?! Why's that?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, she's ordered second-hand oranges for our new client in France.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: That's marvellous… isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I asked her not to. They wanted lemons… new Imperial Lemons.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah… not so marvellous. Anything else?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, speaking personally, I don't think she's pulling her weight. She doesn't seem to do any work and just keeps going out to buy cappuccinos.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Well, that's just not on. Look Anna, I will look into this straight away and see if I can sort this out. Thank you for bringing it to my attention. Now, I think you've earned a custard cream.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: So Anna has expressed her concerns to Paul, the boss. It's up to him to investigate. As long as you have a fair reason to complain about a difficult member of staff, these are some of the phrases you could use:

transcript.speaker: I'm concerned that she's made a mistake that might affect the business.
transcript.text:
She's not pulling her weight.
I'm finding it very difficult to work with her.
I wonder how Paul is going to handle the situation?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah, there you are Rachel. Nice cappuccino? Could you step in to my office for a moment… I'd like a word.

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Ya, sure.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Ooh, I wonder what that's all about. Do you know Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hmm, no idea.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: She's probably going to get a promotion and a pay rise… and a custard cream!

transcript.speaker: Rachel
transcript.text: Thanks Paul, ciao. What a great guy he is. Such a great sense of humour! Looks like we're doing some good work Anna!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Wwwhat?!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh Anna. I'm not sure Paul has really sorted out your concerns. But don't worry, we're here to help you out. See you next time on English at Work. Bye!
